question.leadin: This group mocked the US, France, and UK forces during a mock funeral in Khost.
question.text: Name this group that took over a certain country after defeating a resistance movement in Panjshir Province. This group, which takes its name from the word "students," is largely led by Pashtun militants.
question.clue: This group, the main opponent of the Northern Alliance, carried out the "green on blue" attacks.

swap.text: This man was the greatest expander of the Mongol Empire, conquering territory across China and Central Asia.
swap.clue: The Ilk Khorig, or Great Taboo, may contain this leader's unknown tomb.

question.leadin: This ruler defeated Tokhtamysh [TOKE-TAM-ISH] at the Battle of the Terek River. --.
question.text: Name this conqueror from Samarkand who sacked Damascus and Delhi.
question.clue: This man captured Sultan Bayezid the Thunderbolt at the Battle of Ankara.

swap.text: Along with many explorers before and after him, Ibn Battuta made use of this vast network of land and sea routes which linked Asia, Europe, and Africa.
swap.clue: In the plural, this term was subtitled A New History of the World in a work by Peter Frankopan, and it names Yo-Yo Ma's ensemble to promote cross-cultural artistic collaboration.

question.text: Nevsky maintained a subordinate relationship to this Mongol empire. They fought a civil war against the White Horde and its eastern portion was composed of the Blue Horde.
question.clue: Uzbeg converted it to Islam, less than a century after Batu established it.

swap.text: The Great Cavalry Raid, which was engineered by Subotai, encircled this body of water. Astrakhan lies on this largest lake in the world.
swap.clue: The world's first oil tanker sailed across this body of water from a port that produced half of the world's oil in 1900.

question.leadin: This empire was formed in the 7th century AD following the end of the Zhangzhung kingdom.
question.text: Name this ancient Himalayan empire which flourished until the 9th century and had a capital at Lhasa.
question.clue: Ralpacan was one of this empire's Three Dharma Kings.

swap.text: This Central Asian proxy conflict between the British and Russian empires provided the justification for the war, as the British feared Dost Mohammad Khan would side with the Russians in a potential invasion of India.
swap.clue: The Fortress of Orenburg was constructed in order to control the Kazakhs as part of this period, which also saw extended maneuvering over the rights to Sinkiang.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a certain country.
question.text: Its first namesake war against the British occurred in 1838 when Dost Muhammad was deposed and then restored after a revolution in Kabul.
question.clue: This country's border with its eastern neighbor became the Durand Line after the Treaty of Rawalpindi, and Elphinstone's column was lost on a retreat from this country.

swap.leadin: Vyacheslav Molotov was once placed in virtual exile by being appointed the Soviet Union's ambassador to this Asian country.
swap.text: Identify this country, whose final communist ruler was Jambyn Batmunkh.
swap.clue: The prince Kul Tigin is honored by 7th century inscriptions named for a river valley in this country's west, the Orkhon, which was a power center for the Gokturk state.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the tribe known as the Alans, who migrated to Europe in the late 4th and early 5th centuries.
question.text: In the late 9th century, the Alans established an independent kingdom in this mountain range. A nation in this range is often recognized as the first to establish Christianity as its official religion, doing so in 301 A.D.
question.clue: Gold and silver tubes, possibly used to drink beer, that were found in this region were made by the Maykop culture, which, like this region's Kura-Araxes culture, constructed burial mounds called kurgans.

swap.leadin: The Khoshut Khanate originated the "priest-patron relationship" underlying the Ganden Phodrang system in this region.
swap.text: Name this region where the Mongolian ʼphags-pa script originated. The Khoshut Khan Gushi shared power with the 5th Dalai Lama, who re-established Lhasa as the capital of this region.
swap.answerHtml: Tibet [or Böd or Xīzàng; accept Amdo or Ü Tsang or Kham; accept Tibetan Plateau or Qinghai–Tibet Plateau or Qīng–Zàng Gāoyuán]
swap.clue: The British and Russians competed for control of this region, which achieved de facto independence after the collapse of the Qing Empire.

question.text: Rulers of Rouran used this title that was later adopted by Bumin and the Gokturks. In the 13th century, this title was adopted by Temujin.
question.answerHtml: khan [or khagan; accept Genghis Khan or Chinggis Khan; prompt on emperor]
question.clue: One of these figures destroyed the Khwarezmian cities of Urgench and Samarkand and established his capital at Karakorum.

swap.leadin: A king from this city named Fromo Kesaro, or "Rome Caesar," commemorated his defeat of Yazid ibn Ziyad in his coinage.
swap.text: Name this westernmost capital city home to a Turkic "Shahi" dynasty that expanded to Gandhara. The Turk Shahis likely used the "Bala Hissar" fort in this city, as did the later Hindu Shahis who lost to Mahmud of Ghazni.
swap.clue: A mid-1990s siege of this city culminated in the hanging of former president Mohammad Najibullah outside the Arg Presidential Palace.

question.text: This so-called "Stalin of Mongolia" sought to reunite Outer and Inner Mongolia, but was thwarted by the real Stalin. He served as leader of Mongolia from 1939 to 1952.
question.clue: With Shtern and Zukhov, this man commanded the winning side at the Battle of Khalkin Gol.

swap.leadin: One ruler of this city sentenced two British diplomats to its prison's infamous "bug pit" after they tried to ride into his palace on horseback and arrived without a gift for him.
swap.text: Name this city, the capital of an emirate that lost control of nearby Samarkand when it was attacked by Russia along with the neighboring Khiva and Kokand khanates.
swap.clue: A group modelled off the Young Turks invited the Soviet conquest of this city and was given prominent leadership positions in the short-lived Soviet republic centered on this city.

question.leadin: Original language term required. The holding of two of these events, one held at Kaiping and the other organized by Ariq Boke, led to the Toluid Civil War.
question.text: Name these events, which required commanders like Muqali to pause campaigns and travel hundreds of miles to attend to elect a new Mongol Khan.
question.clue: This meetings at which Great Khans of the Mongol empire were elected in the presence of senior members of each tribe.

swap.text: Setbacks to Dost Muhammad's reign included the capture of this city by the Sikh forces of Ranjit Singh in 1819. This city lies west of the Bara River near the Khyber Pass in the North-West province of modern-day Pakistan.
swap.clue: Pakistan reinstated the death penalty following a Taliban attack on a school in this city on the eastern end of the Khyber Pass. A shrine to its native poet, Rahman Baba, was damaged by a 2009 bombing, presumably also by the Taliban.

question.leadin: Answer the following about British boondoggles in Afghanistan in the 19th century.
question.text: This "line" was set up to divide Afghanistan and British India by an 1893 treaty between the namesake British foreign secretary and the Afghani ruler Amir Abdur Khan. After the partition of India, it became the line between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
question.clue: The creation of this line, named for a British diplomat, effectively created a buffer zone between Britain and Russia in Asia. This line forms the de facto border between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

swap.leadin: In 2013, a seated bronze sculpture of this leader was removed from Mexico City's Paseo de la Reforma, leaving only the stone map of his country behind him.
swap.text: Name this President of Azerbaijan who approved the 1994 Bishkek Protocol to end the First Nagorno-Karabakh War. This man's son Ilham succeeded him shortly before his 2003 death.
swap.answerHtml: Heydar Aliyev [or Heydar Alirza oghlu Aliyev; prompt on just Aliyev]
